item.text: The current exporter uses a package level `sync.Once`, so later calls reuse the first exporter and its configuration. I’ll remove that shared state, keep exporter setup per call, and move the existing gRPC test cases into tracing package tests.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('internal/cmd/grpc_test.go')
s=p.read_text()
a=s.index('func TestGetTraceExporter(')
b=s.index('func TestNewGRPCServer(',a)
s=s[:a]+s[b:]
s=s.replace('\\t\"errors\"\\n','').replace('\\t\"sync\"\\n','')
p.write_text(s)
PY
gofmt -w internal/cmd/grpc.go internal/cmd/grpc_test.go internal/tracing/tracing.go
go test ./internal/tracing ./internal/cmd"

item.text:
Tracing setup now lives in [internal/tracing/tracing.go](/app/internal/tracing/tracing.go). The gRPC server creates the provider through `NewProvider`, obtains an exporter through `GetExporter` when tracing is enabled, and registers both shutdown functions. Exporters are constructed per call, so one configuration no longer controls later calls.

Focused tests cover resource attributes, environment overrides, sampling, exporter types, repeated calls, and invalid OTLP endpoints. `go test ./internal/cmd ./internal/tracing` passes.
